![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/b9f1ea82756eed4a815afb54defd8425631a57a0bcd1dfaba2dbf5b24b43b518.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by $x=y\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ and $x=3\operatorname{ln}⁡y,$ as shown above. Which of the following gives the volume of the solid generated when that region is rotated ${360}^{∘}$ about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(y)=y\operatorname{ln}⁡y$ and $g(y)=3\operatorname{ln}⁡y.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\ y\operatorname{ln}⁡y-3\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =0 \\ (y-3)\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limits of integration are from $y=1$ and $y=3.$ 

Let's draw our horizontal arrow through the region to determine the inner function and the outer function. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14217745/assets/54278318429e01bc3fa2c0325fea7c7a918aacf096b1510d8acc87d3ffc53a73.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner function $x=f(y)=y\operatorname{ln}⁡y,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $x=g(y)=3\operatorname{ln}⁡y.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}([\text{outer}]^{2}-[\text{inner}]^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}({[3\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2}-{[y\operatorname{ln}⁡y]}^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}(9(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)^{2}-{y}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)^{2})\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{3}(9-{y}^{2})(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
